question: On 1 October 2026, the Commission sent a second letter of formal notice to Greece under infringement case INFR(2018)2172, pointing to shortcomings in the alert mechanism provided for in Directive 2005/36/EC.

Notifications are sent through the Internal Market Information System (IMI), informing Member States about professionals who are restricted or banned from practising their profession and about fake education qualifications. According to the Commission, the mechanism is only partially operational in Greece and the information provided to other Member States is insufficient.

The continued imperfect functioning of the system raises serious issues regarding citizen protection, particularly in the fields of health and education. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What specific shortcomings were identified in 2026 and which Greek authorities and professional categories are concerned?
Does it have data on notifications that were either not sent or were sent late by the Greek authorities in the last three years?
What timetable and measurable criteria has it asked Greece to comply with for the mechanism to operate fully?
